Look up the CA bundle in the vendored certifi package.

Upstream passes the top-level name "certifi" to importlib.resources, which would import
the application's certifi (or fail if it isn't installed). __package__ resolves to the
vendored package.

--- a/certifi/core.py
+++ b/certifi/core.py
@@ -37,14 +37,14 @@ if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):
             # We also have to hold onto the actual context manager, because
             # it will do the cleanup whenever it gets garbage collected, so
             # we will also store that at the global level as well.
-            _CACERT_CTX = as_file(files("certifi").joinpath("cacert.pem"))
+            _CACERT_CTX = as_file(files(__package__).joinpath("cacert.pem"))
             _CACERT_PATH = str(_CACERT_CTX.__enter__())
             atexit.register(exit_cacert_ctx)
 
         return _CACERT_PATH
 
     def contents() -> str:
-        return files("certifi").joinpath("cacert.pem").read_text(encoding="ascii")
+        return files(__package__).joinpath("cacert.pem").read_text(encoding="ascii")
 
 else:
 
@@ -73,11 +73,11 @@ else:
             # We also have to hold onto the actual context manager, because
             # it will do the cleanup whenever it gets garbage collected, so
             # we will also store that at the global level as well.
-            _CACERT_CTX = get_path("certifi", "cacert.pem")
+            _CACERT_CTX = get_path(__package__, "cacert.pem")
             _CACERT_PATH = str(_CACERT_CTX.__enter__())
             atexit.register(exit_cacert_ctx)

Default the distro's OTLP protocol to http/protobuf.

The distro defaults OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL to grpc, but the gRPC exporters aren't vendored
(grpcio has no pure-Python wheel). With http/protobuf the SDK resolves the "otlp" exporter to the
vendored otlp_proto_http one. An explicitly set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL still wins.

diff --git a/opentelemetry/distro/__init__.py b/opentelemetry/distro/__init__.py
index 4d00198..6165e7a 100644
--- a/opentelemetry/distro/__init__.py
+++ b/opentelemetry/distro/__init__.py
@@ -28,4 +28,5 @@ class OpenTelemetryDistro(BaseDistro):
         os.environ.setdefault(OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER, "otlp")
         os.environ.setdefault(OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER, "otlp")
         os.environ.setdefault(OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER, "otlp")
-        os.environ.setdefault(OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL, "grpc")
+        # opentelemetry-agent: the gRPC exporters aren't vendored (grpcio has no pure-Python wheel).
+        os.environ.setdefault(OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL, "http/protobuf")

Parse and validate configuration files with ruamel.yaml and fastjsonschema.

opentelemetry-configuration uses pyyaml and jsonschema, which have no pure-Python wheels (jsonschema needs
rpds-py), so they are excluded (vendor-excludes.txt) and the vendored, pure-Python ruamel.yaml and
fastjsonschema stand in for them:

* YAML: ruamel.yaml's PyYAML-style SafeLoader (with the same Node classes, resolve() and
  construct_document()). It resolves scalars with the YAML 1.2 core schema, which the configuration
  spec requires (PyYAML implements YAML 1.1, where e.g. "on" and "no" are booleans).
* Schema: a fastjsonschema validator compiled once. Its draft 2019-09 generator, used for the 2020-12
  $schema, covers every keyword the schema uses ($ref into $defs, oneOf, exclusiveMinimum, ...).
  Errors map to the same ConfigurationError messages.

The schema is also read relative to this file rather than with importlib.resources.files(
"opentelemetry.configuration"), which would resolve the application's package.

Report upstream module names from the vendored SDK.

Instrumentations name their tracers, meters and loggers after their module (get_tracer(__name__)),
which is opentelemetry.agent._vendor.opentelemetry... once vendored. InstrumentationScope (and the
deprecated InstrumentationInfo) strip the vendor prefix, so telemetry reports the same scope names as
the upstream packages, e.g. opentelemetry.instrumentation.aiohttp_client.

The TracerProvider's warning filter for its own InstrumentationInfo deprecation names its module by
string; use __name__ so it matches the vendored module rather than the application's SDK.

             message=(r"You should use InstrumentationScope. Deprecated since version 1.11.1."),

-            module="opentelemetry.sdk.trace",

Scope OpenTelemetry's entry point lookups to the vendored distributions.

All OpenTelemetry plugin discovery (distro, configurator, instrumentors, exporters, samplers,
propagators, resource detectors, HTTP transports) goes through opentelemetry.util._importlib_metadata.
Upstream it reads every installed distribution's entry points: the vendored copies have no
dist-info on sys.path, and the application's OpenTelemetry plugins point at un-vendored modules.
opentelemetry-vendor sync keeps the vendored distributions' METADATA and namespaced entry points in
_vendor/_metadata (metadata-dir); entry_points() and distributions() only search there.

version() and requires() keep looking at the application's distributions: instrumentors check that the
installed version of the library they patch matches their "instruments" requirements.

+++ b/opentelemetry/util/_importlib_metadata.py
@@ -11,38 +11,35 @@ It also normalizes minor differences across python versions 3.10+. References to
 - https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5203
 """
 
-import itertools
+import os
 from functools import cache
 from importlib.metadata import (
     Distribution,
     EntryPoint,
     EntryPoints,
     PackageNotFoundError,
-    distributions,
     requires,
     version,
 )
-from importlib.metadata import entry_points as original_entry_points
-from typing import Any
+from importlib.metadata import distributions as _all_distributions
+from typing import Any, Iterable
+
+# opentelemetry-agent: entry points are only looked up in the vendored distributions' metadata
+# (written to _vendor/_metadata by opentelemetry-vendor sync), never in the application's, whose
+# OpenTelemetry plugins point at un-vendored modules. version() and requires() still see the
+# application's distributions: instrumentors check the installed versions of the libraries they patch.
+_VENDORED_METADATA_PATH = [
+    os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))), "_metadata")
+]
 
 
-def _as_entry_points(eps: Any) -> EntryPoints:
-    # Python versions greater than 3.11 return EntryPoints.
-    if isinstance(eps, EntryPoints):
-        return eps
-    # In Python 3.10 and 3.11 entry_points() returns
-    # a dict-like SelectableGroups object.
-    # Use dict.values() instead of eps.values() to avoid the DeprecationWarning
-    # that SelectableGroups raises when calling .values().
-    if isinstance(eps, dict):
-        return EntryPoints(itertools.chain.from_iterable(dict.values(eps)))
-    # This case should be unreachable, but is included as a fallback.
-    return EntryPoints(ep for group in eps.groups for ep in eps.select(group=group))
+def distributions(**kwargs: Any) -> Iterable[Distribution]:
+    return _all_distributions(path=_VENDORED_METADATA_PATH, **kwargs)
 
 
 @cache
 def _original_entry_points_cached() -> EntryPoints:
-    return _as_entry_points(original_entry_points())
+    return EntryPoints(entry_point for dist in distributions() for entry_point in dist.entry_points)

Select the vendored protobuf implementation: upb when built, else pure Python.

Upstream probes for the upb/cpp C extensions with importlib.import_module("google._upb._message")
and friends, which imports the application's protobuf by its top-level name, and honours
PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION, which is meant for the application's protobuf: "cpp" makes
descriptor.py import the missing vendored pyext and crash. Only the vendored upb extension (included in
platform builds of the agent, see patches/native/protobuf-upb.patch) is considered; otherwise the
pure-Python implementation is used.

Disable the requests.packages compatibility aliases.

Upstream imports urllib3/idna/chardet by their top-level names and registers them as
`requests.packages.*` in the global sys.modules, which would load and alias the
application's own packages.

diff --git a/requests/packages.py b/requests/packages.py
--- a/requests/packages.py
+++ b/requests/packages.py
@@ -1,23 +1,4 @@
-import sys
-
-from .compat import chardet
-
-# This code exists for backwards compatibility reasons.
-# I don't like it either. Just look the other way. :)
-
-for package in ("urllib3", "idna"):
-    locals()[package] = __import__(package)
-    # This traversal is apparently necessary such that the identities are
-    # preserved (requests.packages.urllib3.* is urllib3.*)
-    for mod in list(sys.modules):
-        if mod == package or mod.startswith(f"{package}."):
-            sys.modules[f"requests.packages.{mod}"] = sys.modules[mod]
-
-if chardet is not None:
-    target = chardet.__name__
-    for mod in list(sys.modules):
-        if mod == target or mod.startswith(f"{target}."):
-            imported_mod = sys.modules[mod]
-            sys.modules[f"requests.packages.{mod}"] = imported_mod
-            mod = mod.replace(target, "chardet")
-            sys.modules[f"requests.packages.{mod}"] = imported_mod
+# The upstream module imports urllib3, idna and chardet by their top-level names and
+# registers them as `requests.packages.*` in the global sys.modules. In the vendored copy
+# that would load (and alias) the application's own packages, so the backwards
+# compatibility aliases are disabled.

Never load the libyaml binding in the vendored ruamel.yaml.

ruamel.yaml imports the optional C parser and emitter from the _ruamel_yaml extension module
(ruamel.yaml.clib), which would be the application's, not vendored. ruamel/yaml/cyaml.py is dropped; this
patch makes main.py fall back to the pure-Python implementation unconditionally.

diff --git a/ruamel/yaml/main.py b/ruamel/yaml/main.py
index fdf7c72..5e23910 100644
--- a/ruamel/yaml/main.py
+++ b/ruamel/yaml/main.py
@@ -42,10 +42,9 @@ if False:  # MYPY
     from types import TracebackType
     from pathlib import Path
 
-try:
-    from _ruamel_yaml import CParser, CEmitter  # type: ignore
-except:  # NOQA
-    CParser = CEmitter = None
+# opentelemetry-agent: always use the pure-Python parser and emitter; the libyaml binding
+# (_ruamel_yaml) would be the application's, not vendored.
+CParser = CEmitter = None
 
 # import io
